title: Pairwise lattice breakdown for onboarding: multi-metric bakeoff (Sep 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This note captures the pairwise-lattice experiment we ran to compare a small candidate set of variants for onboarding into the hosted model catalog. The goal was to produce a high-confidence ordering across multiple axes (response quality, stability, latency, and unit cost) using dense pairwise comparisons rather than a single scalar leaderboard. This is intended to supplement the existing eval dashboards with a more interpretable win/loss lattice for rollout decisions.

Scope and hypothesis:
- Candidate set: four variants targeted for production onboarding in Q4 2026. Names below are shorthand used throughout the experiment.
- Hypothesis: a quantile-based affinity scoring of pairwise outcomes will surface a single runner-up model that balances quality vs cost while keeping latency within current SLOs. We expected the Redwood compact quantized variant to trade a measurable quality delta for a ~40% cost reduction and ~15% latency improvement.

Candidates (short names used in tables):
- R-clarity-1.1 (baseline high-quality variant; FP16)
- OC-13B-q4 (open checkpoint, 13B q4_0)
- R-compact-2.0-4bit (Redwood compact quantized, 4-bit)
- GPTX-7B-slim (third-party light variant, FP16 fused kernels)

Prompt sets used (representative mix):
- edge-commons-280: short-form QA + API doc summarization (280 prompts)
- safety-qa-lite: 120 safety-related adversarial prompts
- doc-synth-structured-v2: 90 structured extraction/format tasks
- chatty-agent-stress-50: 50 multi-turn conversational continuations

Evaluation methodology (pairwise lattice):
1) For each prompt, we generate outputs from all candidates with fixed decoding seeds and identical sampling params.
2) Human raters (n=6 rotation) perform blind pairwise judgements for random pairs of outputs for the same prompt. Judgements recorded as: A better / B better / tie / unacceptable.
3) We compute pairwise win rates (A beats B excluding ties) and an "affinity score" for each model as the average of its win rates against others weighted by stability factor (inverse of rater disagreement).
4) Secondary metrics collected per-output: latency (p50/p95), tokens generated, and cost estimate (approx $/1k tokens using current infra unit-cost model).
5) We also measure regression signal against a small holdout promptset of high-sensitivity prompts (safety + legal phrasing).

Notes on rater protocol and QA:
- Raters flagged hallucination/high-certainty wrong answers separately; these count as losses for the producing model regardless of other peripheral strengths.
- Inter-rater agreement (Kripp alpha) computed per prompt set to sanity-check stability; sets with alpha < 0.25 were downweighted in affinity.
pairwise_matrix:
Pairwise win rates (percent A beats B; ties excluded) - aggregated across all prompt sets:

           R-clarity-1.1  OC-13B-q4  R-compact-2.0-4bit  GPTX-7B-slim
R-clarity-1.1      -            62.4%            71.9%             58.1%
OC-13B-q4          37.6%           -             49.2%             45.0%
R-compact-2.0-4bit 28.1%         50.8%              -              39.5%
GPTX-7B-slim       41.9%         55.0%             60.5%              -

Observations:
- R-clarity dominates in raw quality win rate vs compact and OC-13B.
- OC-13B is competitive with R-compact on quality, slight edge to OC overall on some prompt families (factual QA).
- GPTX-7B shows mixed results: loses to R-clarity but often beats OC-13B and R-compact on conversational fluency but exhibits higher hallucination counts on structured extraction tasks.
leaderboards:
Condensed leaderboard (affinity-weighted) and cost/latency summary:

Model | affinity_score | avg_rank | overall_win_rate | p50_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | est_cost_per_1k_tokens
R-clarity-1.1 | 0.78 | 1.2 | 64.1% | 210 ms | 520 ms | $9.20
OC-13B-q4     | 0.46 | 2.1 | 47.6% | 180 ms | 430 ms | $4.10
R-compact-2.0-4bit | 0.52 | 2.0 | 53.6% | 160 ms | 360 ms | $2.45
GPTX-7B-slim  | 0.41 | 3.3 | 46.2% | 170 ms | 410 ms | $3.90

Key takeaways from leaderboard:
- R-clarity is the quality leader but ~3.8x more expensive than R-compact per 1k tokens.
- R-compact achieves the best balance of cost and latency with a modest quality gap vs R-clarity; it outperforms OC-13B on affinity despite similar raw win rates because of superior stability (lower inter-rater disagreement).
- GPTX-7B's higher hallucination incidents reduce its effective affinity despite decent fluency scores.
decision:
Recommendation (proposed for product onboarding):
Primary recommendation: Move R-compact-2.0-4bit into the beta slot for hosted / dedicated onboarding with the following guardrails:
- Start with canary traffic at 10% for latency-sensitive endpoints and 25% for non-critical batch endpoints.
- Attach automatic rollback if hallucination/unacceptable rate exceeds baseline R-clarity by +1.5 percentage points over a 24h window.
- Enable prefix caching and RL-config quant-aware padding to preserve latency SLOs.
Rationale: R-compact provides a 58% median reduction in estimated unit cost vs R-clarity while keeping average quality within an acceptable band. Its stability profile (lower rater disagreement, fewer micro-regressions on structured tasks) reduces operational risk compared to OC-13B.
Fallback: If production safety holdout triggers more than +0.8% unacceptable answers, demote to a reduced footprint dedicated pool and fallback to R-clarity for affected routes.
Incremental steps:
1) Weaponize the existing promptset subset for continuous quality monitoring (edge-commons-280 slices + safety-qa-lite).
2) Run a 72-hour mini-shadow with real traffic tokens counted for cost calibration.
3) Final go/no-go after 7 days of canary with telemetry: human-spotted hallucination rate, latency SLOs, and cost delta validated against billing estimate.
notes:
Anomalies and open questions:
- OC-13B outperformed expectations on factual QA but struggled on structured extraction; need to inspect tokenizer differences and special-casing for numeric tables. Could be a data alignment artifact.
- R-compact showed occasional label-preserving hallucinations (plausible but wrong) in safety-qa-lite that were borderline for raters; we should add targeted prompts to the safety holdout.
- GPTX-7B has attractive latency but inconsistent hallucination profiles; consider further ablation with temperature and top-p constraints.

Next actions (owners):
- Priya: schedule 72h mini-shadow and attach monitoring dashboards (AM-8421)
- David: investigate OC-13B tokenizer mismatch and run tokenization parity tests (GH PR #312)
- Sofia: extend safety holdout with 30 targeted prompts and rerun pairwise checks
- Liam: prepare rollout config and automated rollback policy in the console (canary + auto-fallback)

Appendix: raw rater agreement by prompt set (Kripp alpha): edge-commons-280: 0.41, safety-qa-lite: 0.33, doc-synth-structured-v2: 0.27, chatty-agent-stress-50: 0.36. We downweighted doc-synth by 0.6 in affinity due to lower alpha.

Rater notes snippets (selected):
- "R-clarity is consistently more precise on long-form synthesis but sometimes over-explains."
- "R-compact tends to drop decimal precision in tables; otherwise concise and fast."
- "GPTX-7B replies are smooth but occasionally invents plausible-sounding names on legal prompts."

This doc is the working decision memo for the applied-ml onboarding thread. Please leave comments on the linked PR or drop notes in #am-onboard for anything that should change before final approval.
